question:
A four-product T-shirt/sweatshirt manufacturing company must complete production within 72 hours. The truck capacity is limited to 1,200 standard-sized boxes, with each standard box holding 12 T-shirts. A box for a dozen sweatshirts is three times the size of a standard box. With $25,000 available for a production run and 500 dozen blank T-shirts and sweatshirts in stock, determine how many dozens (boxes) of each type of shirt should be produced to maximize profit. Consider the following table for resource requirements for the product mix.

Table (Resource requirements per dozen of each product type):
| Product Type | Processing Time (hr/dozen) | Cost ($/dozen) | Profit ($/dozen) |
| ------------ | -------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------- |
| Sweatshirt - F | 0.10 | $36 | $90 |
| Sweatshirt - B/F | 0.25 | $48 | $125 |
| T-shirt - F | 0.08 | $25 | $45 |
| T-shirt - B/F | 0.21 | $35 | $65 |

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "products": ["S_F", "S_BF", "T_F", "T_BF"],
    "time":    {"S_F": 0.10, "S_BF": 0.25, "T_F": 0.08, "T_BF": 0.21},   # hr/dozen
    "cost":    {"S_F": 36,   "S_BF": 48,   "T_F": 25,   "T_BF": 35},     # $/dozen
    "profit":  {"S_F": 90,   "S_BF": 125,  "T_F": 45,   "T_BF": 65},     # $/dozen
    "box_size": {"S_F": 3, "S_BF": 3, "T_F": 1, "T_BF": 1},              # standard boxes per dozen
    "time_avail": 72,       # hours
    "budget_avail": 25000,  # dollars
    "stock_avail": 500,     # dozen blanks
    "truck_capacity": 1200  # standard boxes
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])

    # x[p] = dozens produced of product p (integer, >= 0)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Processing time: sum(time_p * x_p) <= time_avail
    def time_rule(m):
        return sum(d["time"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["time_avail"]
    model.time_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=time_rule)

    # Budget: sum(cost_p * x_p) <= budget_avail
    def budget_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cost"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["budget_avail"]
    model.budget_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=budget_rule)

    # Stock: total dozens <= stock_avail
    def stock_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["stock_avail"]
    model.stock_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=stock_rule)

    # Truck capacity: sum(box_size_p * x_p) <= truck_capacity
    def truck_rule(m):
        return sum(d["box_size"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["truck_capacity"]
    model.truck_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=truck_rule)

    # Objective: maximize total profit
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["profit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model


if __name__ == "__main__":

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Problem: four-product T-shirt / sweatshirt production mix
#
# Decision variables (all indexed by product p in P = {SF, SBF, TF, TBF}):
#   x[p] : dozens of product p to produce
#          domain: NonNegativeIntegers (quantities are whole dozens)
#
# Objective (maximize):
#   total profit = sum_p profit[p] * x[p]
#
# Constraints:
#   1) Processing time limit (source: "must complete production within 72 hours")
#        sum_p time[p] * x[p] <= 72
#   2) Budget limit (source: "$25,000 available for a production run")
#        sum_p cost[p] * x[p] <= 25000
#   3) Truck capacity in standard-box equivalents
#      (source: "truck capacity limited to 1,200 standard-sized boxes";
#       a standard box holds 12 T-shirts = 1 dozen; a sweatshirt box is
#       three times the size of a standard box)
#        sum_p boxfactor[p] * x[p] <= 1200
#   4) Blank stock limit (source: "500 dozen blank T-shirts and sweatshirts
#      in stock")
#        sum_p x[p] <= 500
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "products": ["SF", "SBF", "TF", "TBF"],
    # processing time (hr per dozen)
    "time": {"SF": 0.10, "SBF": 0.25, "TF": 0.08, "TBF": 0.21},
    # cost ($ per dozen)
    "cost": {"SF": 36, "SBF": 48, "TF": 25, "TBF": 35},
    # profit ($ per dozen)
    "profit": {"SF": 90, "SBF": 125, "TF": 45, "TBF": 65},
    # standard-box equivalents per dozen (sweatshirts = 3x standard box)
    "boxfactor": {"SF": 3, "SBF": 3, "TF": 1, "TBF": 1},
    # resource limits
    "time_limit": 72,
    "budget_limit": 25000,
    "truck_capacity": 1200,
    "blank_stock": 500,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = d["products"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    def profit_rule(m):
        return sum(d["profit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=profit_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    def time_rule(m):
        return sum(d["time"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["time_limit"]

    model.time_limit_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=time_rule)

    def budget_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cost"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["budget_limit"]

    model.budget_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=budget_rule)

    def truck_rule(m):
        return sum(d["boxfactor"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["truck_capacity"]

    model.truck_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=truck_rule)

    def stock_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["blank_stock"]

    model.stock_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=stock_rule)

    return model
